direct, selective photostimulation of hypocretin (Hcr) neurons in the lateral (LH) hypothalamus increases the probability of transition from either slow wave (SWS) or rapid eye movement (REM) sleep to wakefulness.

direct, selective optogenetic phototstimulation of hypocretin (Hcr) neurons in the lateral (posterior) hypothalamus of freely moving mice increases the probability of transition from slow wave sleep (SWS) and rapid eye movement (REM) sleep to the awake state, and that the frequency of the Hcr photostimulus is an important determinant of this effect.

optogenetic activation of Hcrt cells increases the probability of transition from both REM and NREM sleep to wakefulness, and that this is most effective when the light pulses are delivered at a frequency of 5–30 pulses per second.
